title: Bastion/proxy credential rotation & liveness sieve for air-gapped Private customers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers using Private/VPC and air-gapped deployments have reported operational risk during periodic bastion/proxy credential rotations (bastion keys, proxy certs, connector tokens). Current process requires manual ops windows or network egress changes which is unacceptable for isolation-sensitive customers. This ticket scopes a triage and implementation plan for a self-serve 'rotation + liveness sieve' that: 1) detects stale/expiring credentials early, 2) orchestrates rotation with zero-touch where possible (customer opt-in), 3) provides clear rollback and observability, and 4) defines gated exceptions for air-gapped environments that cannot accept outbound calls during rotation windows.
acceptance_criteria: Define detection heuristics and liveness probes for bastion/proxy credentials usable across common connector patterns (SSH bastion, TLS certs, service tokens)

Provide a documented rotation flow for customers that supports (a) zero-touch rotation via scheduled update with customer-signed bundle, (b) assisted rotation with ephemeral egress window, and (c) fully offline/manual rotation guidance
Console UI: expose rotation status per-tenant with next-expiry, last-rotation, and recommended action
Automation: safe-rollout playbook implemented for Dedicated and Private control planes with canary policy and automatic rollback on liveness failure
Playbook: escalation steps, runbook commands, and a post-rotation verification checklist exist in Confluence
No customer downtime during certified zero-touch rotations in at least two pilot customers (internal test + 1 paying customer)
Telemetry: rotation attempts, failures, and liveness probe results emitted to runtime-telemetry with dashboards and alerts
notes: 2026-03-01: Intake call with security, infra, and 3 customers (BankCo, HealthSys, RetailAI). Customers flagged tightening audit windows and inability to open egress for scheduled rotations.
2026-03-03: Engineering spike completed: identified three connector classes and corresponding rotation primitives. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bastion-rotation-spike/pull/12

2026-03-05: Design mockup for Console status card reviewed; feedback: add explicit 'airgap advisory' badge and a stepper for manual rotation flow. Mockup link: https://drive.redwood.com/designs/bastion-rotation-v1
2026-03-07: Security clarified that customer-managed KMS integrations require signature verification step for zero-touch bundles; added to requirements
2026-03-09: Agreement in cross-functional sync: pilot with BankCo (will accept ephemeral egress), HealthSys will need fully offline manual rotation path. Plan to run pilot in Cycle 10
decisions: Use a hybrid approach: prefer zero-touch where a signed rotation bundle (customer-provided) can be delivered via existing connector, otherwise fall back to assisted ephemeral egress
Liveness probes will be idempotent and light-weight (TCP handshake + TLS verify + token exchange), with configurable thresholds per customer
Rotation orchestration will live in private-control-plane service 'rotor', integrated with existing rollout and canary infra
We will not require upstream changes from customers for pilot; where customer constraints demand, provide scripted manual steps and validation artifacts
risks: Air-gapped customers with strict no-egress policies may still require on-site operator involvement; increases time-to-rotate and operational cost
Incorrect liveness heuristics risk false negatives (thinking rotation succeeded) — mitigated by multi-step verification and short canary windows
Credential rotation automation increases blast radius if orchestration bugs not fully validated — we will run staged canaries and include automatic rollback triggers
